targets.why: The cheapest number on the page. 208 finishers had no activity logged at all; converting one in five turns the book from −4.6 to +1.4 a month. Nothing else stabilises revenue this cheaply.
Holds the book flat alongside an 80% extension rate, and gives headroom to rebuild toward the Oct–May run-rate.

targets.metric: CVs sent per head per working day
targets.why: The earliest reliably-logged stage, so it is the only safe anchor. +39% CVs at today's unchanged conversion is what funds the placement target.
Below 2.0 means steps are being skipped. Getting to 3.0 on the SAME jobs is worth about +129 placements a year with no new BD at all.
A-jobs fill at 32% against 5.6% for everything else — a 5.7× gap. This is a qualification discipline, not more calls.
Restoring the 2022–25 level is worth roughly €1.5M a year on the same volume. Start with UCB, Electrabel, Belfius and AG Insurance, all running 11–12.6%.
85% of new candidates are never sent to a job or contact. This is sourcing effort already paid for and thrown away.
Was 110% three years ago. Either the checks stopped or the logging did, and one of those is a compliance exposure, not a KPI.

yoy: CV→placement conversion over the same span

crm.why: Every ratio, cohort and forecast in this analysis comes from stage entries. Storing only current status makes all of it impossible to reproduce — and you will not find out until Cube19 is gone.

crm.what: Extension / end-date alerting on every live assignment
crm.why: 56% of finishers had no logged activity. This one screen is worth more than the rest of the CRM combined and is a few days of work.

crm.what: Mandatory owner on every placement — no placeholders
crm.why: 36% of contract placements sit on Ghost_* owners holding 14% of GP. Every leaderboard and commission number is wrong by that margin.

crm.what: Job qualification grade, required before a CV can be sent
crm.why: A-jobs fill 5.7× better, but 16% of placements carry no grade at all. Make the grade a gate, not a field.
26% of contract placements are below 12%. Catch it when the rate is agreed, not in a quarterly review.

crm.what: Stable desk taxonomy with a historical crosswalk
crm.why: Retired [deleted] groups, compound desks later split, and 'Gentis Consultancy' as a catch-all all break year-on-year comparison permanently.
Without it you cannot separate 'the business shrank' from 'the team shrank'. Cube19 never captured it and that is why the last four years are ambiguous.

crm.what: Retainers and spec sends as their own record types
crm.why: 12% of 'placements' are retainer bookings that never needed a CV. They inflate placement counts and flatter every conversion ratio.
Genuinely the easy part, and the part to build LAST. It is arithmetic over the model above — the engine in this repo already does it.
